title: Compliance milestone chaos testing and rollback playbook
creator: Morgan Patel
description: Create and track a validated set of chaos tests and a prescriptive rollback playbook tied to major compliance milestones (SOC2/ISO, SSO cutovers, audit-log retention changes). The goal is to ensure we can safely execute risky operational changes during sprint windows while preserving evidence for audits and minimizing customer impact.
updates: 2026-02-18: Draft playbook skeleton completed. Mapped primary failure modes for SSO cutover and audit-log retention switch (auth path, KMS access, log pipeline backpressure).
2026-02-26: Eng spike (ENG-22478) showed KV cache warmup causes ~10% request failures under synthetic traffic; mitigation candidates documented.
2026-03-03: Legal & Compliance reviewed evidence buckets. Added explicit retention-proof step and signed timestamp requirement. Action: PM to add Confluence evidence template.

2026-03-07: SRE ran first low-risk chaos run in staging (partial auth DB outage). Observed fallback to cached sessions as expected. Logged metrics to compliance dashboard: auth_error_rate, failed_log_ingest, tail_latency.
2026-03-10: Risk threshold table finalized. Playbook now includes immediate rollback triggers and soft-fallback path for degraded audit-log writes.
decisions: Decision: Use staged chaos tests (staging -> canary -> gradual production) tied to milestone gates to reduce audit evidence churn.
Decision: Rollbacks should favor data-preservation first (quiesce writes) then full rollback. Never drop logs that could be required for evidence.
Decision: For SSO/SAML rotations, we require an on-call cross-functional approver (PM + SRE + Security) before proceeding to production canary.
Decision: Automate evidence capture (signed manifest + snapshot) after each test run to attach to SOC2 evidence bucket.

acceptance_criteria: A1: Three representative chaos scenarios run in staging with automated evidence captured and attached to Confluence page.
A2: Canary run executed with no >1% customer-impacting errors and SLA fallback behaviors exercised.
A3: Rollback playbook executed in a dry-run and rollback automation validated in canary cluster.
A4: Compliance confirms that captured artifacts meet SOC2/ISO evidence requirements (signed manifests, timestamps, logs).
rollback_playbook: Step 1: Immediately cut new traffic to canary using routing policy (console route toggle). Document exact timestamp and operator.
Step 2: Quiesce write paths related to audit-logs and persist buffered events to immutable archive (S3 with WORM policy).
Step 3: Execute targeted rollback for the last change (revert deployment via GitHub PR revert). Record PR link in evidence manifest.
Step 4: If rollback not possible within 15 minutes, invoke soft-fallback: route to compatible model variant or fallback region and enable degraded-mode flags.
Step 5: After service stabilization, run postmortem checklist: collect logs, describe impact, attach signed evidence, notify stakeholders and Compliance ops.
chaos_test_plan: Scenario A - SSO key rotation failure: simulate KMS latency and replay stale SAML assertions; verify session fallback and user-visible errors.
Scenario B - Audit log pipeline backpressure: throttle log sink to simulate retention lag and ensure buffered queue persists events to archive.
Scenario C - Partial auth DB outage: kill 10% of auth replicas and confirm circuit-breaker behavior and failover timelines.
Execution cadence: staging (weekly), canary (after gate approval), production progressive (0.1% -> 1% -> 10%)
Observability: baseline and deviation windows defined for each metric (error_rate, p95 latency, log_ingest_lag).
evidence_requirements: Signed manifest file with operator, timestamp, and git commit IDs for code/config changes.
Snapshot of metrics dashboard around test window (PNG) and raw metric export (CSV).
Archived log bundle for affected services (s3 path) including audit-log writes and ingress traces.
Post-run approval email or ticket from Compliance confirming artifact sufficiency.
risks: Risk: Overzealous chaos runs could generate spurious audit evidence that increases compliance workload. Mitigation: restrict artifact capture windows and add metadata tags.
Risk: Rollback automation might not cover edge-case migrations (schema changes). Mitigation: require manual approval for DB-affecting changes.
Risk: Evidence storage cost could grow if we archive full bundles each run. Mitigation: compress bundles and keep retention aligned with audit needs.
